newsitem.title: USA: Half of leaders leaving U.S. House ag panel.
newsitem.headline: Half of leaders leaving U.S. House ag panel.

text.p: Seven of the 12 leaders on the U.S. House Agriculture Committee will be gone when the new Congress meets, mostly to retirement or the Senate, election results showed Friday.
Missouri Democrat Harold Volkmer was the only one to lose re-election. He was defeated by Kenny Hulshof, a Republican, by 7,000 votes.

Elected to the Senate were chairman Pat Roberts, Kansas Republican; Colorado Republican Wayne Allard, chairman of the conservation subcommittee; and Tim Johnson of South Dakota, the Democratic leader on the conservation subcommittee.

Retiring were Kika de la Garza of Texas, former committee chairman and the panel's Democratic leader since 1994, as well as livestock subcommittee chairman Steve Gunderson, Wisconsin Republican, and Charlie Rose of North Carolina, the Democratic leader on the specialty crop subcommittee.
